title: Scale Factor, Area and Volume — Year 9

header.title: Scale Factor, Area and Volume
header.subtitle: Lengths × k, areas × k², volumes × k³

meta.lesson-focus: Investigate how enlargement by scale factor k affects area (× k²) and volume (× k³); compare side lengths, areas and volumes of similar squares and cubes for k = 2, 3, and fractional k; generalise the pattern to any similar 2D and 3D shape.
meta.ac9-descriptor-text: apply the enlargement transformation to shapes and objects using dynamic geometry software as appropriate; identify and explain aspects that remain the same and those that change
meta.sa-conceptual-understanding: Trigonometric ratios are an application of the property of similarity for right-angled triangles

html.section0_intro: Three quick questions on scale factors, area and volume. Last lesson every length was multiplied by k. Today: what happens to area and volume?
html.section_warmup:
A real situation that is secretly today's mathematics.

A pizza shop sells a 20 cm pizza for $10 and a 40 cm pizza for $30. The big one is twice as wide but three times the price. Is that a rip-off?

Doubling the diameter doubles every length across the pizza: it is 2 times as wide left-to-right and 2 times as wide front-to-back. So it has 2 × 2 = 4 times the area. You pay 3 times the price for 4 times the food, so the big pizza is the better value.

Today: when every length is multiplied by a scale factor k, what happens to area and to volume?

💡 Lengths × 2, but area × 4. Price per cm² is what matters.
html.vocab_cards:
Scale factor k
Tap to flip
The number every length is multiplied by in an enlargement.
k = 3: a 2 cm edge becomes 6 cm.
Similar
Tap to flip
Same shape, different size. Every length is multiplied by the same scale factor and angles are unchanged.
Any two squares, any two cubes, any two circles.
Area factor
Tap to flip
The number the area is multiplied by. For scale factor k, the area factor is k2.
k = 3 → area × 9
Volume factor
Tap to flip
The number the volume is multiplied by. For scale factor k, the volume factor is k3.
k = 3 → volume × 27
Dimensions
Tap to flip
Length has 1 dimension, area has 2 and volume has 3. Each dimension is multiplied by k.
cm → cm2 → cm3
html.section3_desc: A box is enlarged with scale factor k = 3. Drag each measurement into the bucket that shows what it is multiplied by.
html.sort_activity:
A box is enlarged with scale factor k = 3
Edge length Area of one face Volume Height Total surface area Capacity in litres Perimeter of one face Paint needed to cover it Mass (same material) Diagonal of a face

× 3 (length)

× 9 (area)

× 27 (volume)

💡 Ask: what units is it measured in? cm → × k. cm2 → × k2. cm3 (or litres, or kilograms of the same material) → × k3.
html.worked_example:
A square of side 2 cm and a cube of edge 2 cm are both enlarged with scale factor k = 3. How many times bigger is the area of the square? The volume of the cube?

1
Multiply every length by k
Every length is 3 times as long, so the square's side and the cube's edge both become 2 × 3 = 6 cm.
side: 2 cm → 6 cm  ·  edge: 2 cm → 6 cm
2
Area: two lengths, so × k × k
The width is × 3 and the height is × 3. The thick lines show the original square fits 9 times into the image.
22 = 4 cm2 → 62 = (3 × 2)2 = 32 × 22 = 36 cm2  ·  36 ÷ 4 = 9 = 32
3
Volume: three lengths, so × k × k × k
Length, width and height are each × 3. Count the layers: 6 layers of 6 × 6 unit cubes.
23 = 8 cm3 → 63 = 33 × 23 = 216 cm3  ·  216 ÷ 8 = 27 = 33
Answer Lengths × 3, area × 32 = 9, volume × 33 = 27. In general: lengths × k, area × k2, volume × k3.
html.we_do_intro: A square of side 4 cm and a cube of edge 4 cm are both reduced with scale factor k = 12. Every length is halved. Fractions can be typed like 1/4.
html.strategy_section:
★Always, sometimes or never?

Each claim is about enlarging a shape or solid with scale factor k. Drag it into the bucket where it belongs. Wrong drops shake back. For a sometimes claim, find a value of k that makes it true and one that makes it false.

Enlarging with k = 3 multiplies the area by 9 Doubling every length of a solid doubles its volume The image has a bigger area than the original If every length is doubled, the volume is multiplied by 8 The volume factor is bigger than the area factor Halving every length of a cube halves its volume The area factor equals the scale factor Angles stay the same in an enlargement Enlarging a cube with k = 2 multiplies its surface area by 8

✓ Always true

~ Sometimes true

✗ Never true

💡 The sometimes claims depend on k. A bigger area needs k > 1 (with k = 12 the area is × 14). The volume factor k3 beats the area factor k2 only when k > 1. And k2 = k only when k = 1, an identical copy.

★Hinge check 🎯 Pick one

A storage box is enlarged so that every length is doubled. The original box holds 10 litres. How much does the new box hold?

You multiplied by k = 2. That only works for lengths. Capacity is a volume: length, width and height are all doubled.
You used the area factor k2 = 4. Capacity has three dimensions, not two. Use k3.
You multiplied by 2 × 3 = 6. Three dimensions means 2 × 2 × 2, not 2 × 3.
Correct. Volume factor = 23 = 8, so 10 × 8 = 80 litres.

retrieval.q: A rectangle's 4 cm side becomes 10 cm in a similar, larger rectangle. What is the scale factor?
retrieval.hint: Scale factor = image length ÷ original length = 10 ÷ 4.

fb.6: You found the difference (10 − 4). A scale factor multiplies: what times 4 gives 10?

retrieval.q: What is the area of a square with side 6 cm, in cm<sup>2</sup>?
retrieval.hint: Area of a square = side × side.

fb.24: That is the perimeter (4 × 6). Area is side × side.

retrieval.q: What is the volume of a cube with edge 3 cm, in cm<sup>3</sup>?
retrieval.hint: Volume of a cube = edge × edge × edge.

fb.9: That is the area of one face. Volume needs three lengths: 3 × 3 × 3.

weDo.q: The 4 cm square becomes a 2 cm square. What is its new area, in cm<sup>2</sup>?

fb.8: That is half of 16. Both the width and the height were halved: 2 × 2.

weDo.q: The original area was 16 cm<sup>2</sup>. What fraction of the original area is the new area?
weDo.hint: 4 ÷ 16, which is also (12)2.

fb.1/2: That is the scale factor. Area has two dimensions: ½ × ½.

weDo.q: The 4 cm cube becomes a 2 cm cube. Its volume was 64 cm<sup>3</sup>. What is its new volume, in cm<sup>3</sup>?
weDo.hint: 2 × 2 × 2, or 64 × (12)3 = 64 × 18.

fb.32: That halves the volume. All three dimensions were halved: 64 × ⅛.
fb.16: That uses the area factor ¼. Volume has three dimensions: 64 × ⅛.

checkpoint.q: A shape is enlarged with scale factor k = 4. The area is multiplied by what number?

fb.4: That is the scale factor. Area has two dimensions, so multiply by k × k.
fb.8: You doubled k. The area factor is k × k = 4 × 4.

checkpoint.q: A solid has volume 6 cm3. It is enlarged with k = 2. What is the new volume, in cm3?

fb.12: You multiplied by k. Volume has three dimensions: multiply by 2 × 2 × 2.
fb.24: You used the area factor 4. Volume needs k³ = 8.

practice1.q: A square with side 3 cm is enlarged with k = 4. What is the area of the image, in cm2?

fb.36: You multiplied the area by k. The area factor is k² = 16.

practice1.q: A shape is enlarged with k = 5. The area is multiplied by what number?

fb.5: That is the scale factor. Area has two dimensions, so multiply by k × k.

practice1.q: A solid is enlarged with k = 2. The volume is multiplied by what number?

fb.4: That is the area factor. Volume has three dimensions: k³.

practice1.q: A cube with edge 2 cm is enlarged with k = 4. What is the volume of the image, in cm3?

fb.32: You multiplied the volume by k. The volume factor is k³ = 64.

practice1.q: A rectangle measuring 3 cm by 5 cm is enlarged with k = 2. What is the area of the image, in cm2?
practice1.hint: New rectangle is 6 cm by 10 cm. (Or 15 × 2<sup>2</sup>.)

fb.30: You doubled the area. Both sides doubled, so the area is × 4.

practice1.q: A shape has area 7 cm2. It is enlarged with k = 3. What is the area of the image, in cm2?

fb.21: You multiplied by k. Area factor is k² = 9.

practice1.q: A solid has volume 5 cm3. It is enlarged with k = 3. What is the volume of the image, in cm3?

fb.15: You multiplied by k. Volume factor is k³ = 27.
fb.45: You used the area factor 9. Volume factor is k³ = 27.

practice1.q: A shape is reduced with k = 12. The area is multiplied by what number? Type a fraction or decimal.
practice1.hint: (12)2 = 12 × 12.

fb.1/2: That is the scale factor. Area factor is ½ × ½.

practice1.q: A solid is enlarged with k = 10. The volume is multiplied by what number?

fb.100: That is the area factor. Volume factor is 10³.

practice1.q: A triangle has area 12 cm2. It is reduced with k = 12. What is the area of the image, in cm2?
practice1.hint: Area factor = (12)2 = 14. Then 12 × 14.

fb.6: You halved the area. Base and height are both halved: area × ¼.

practice2.q: A shape is enlarged with k = 1.5. The area is multiplied by what number?

fb.1.5: That is the scale factor. Area has two dimensions, so multiply by k × k.

practice2.q: A cylinder is reduced with k = 23. The volume is multiplied by what fraction?
practice2.hint: (23)3 = 2 × 2 × 23 × 3 × 3.

fb.4/9: That is the area factor. Volume factor is (2/3)³.
fb.2/9: Cube the top and the bottom: 2³ over 3³.

practice2.q: A circle has area 50 cm<sup>2</sup>. Its radius is doubled. What is the new area, in cm<sup>2</sup>?
practice2.hint: Doubling the radius is an enlargement with k = 2, so area × 4. (No π needed.)

fb.100: You doubled the area. Every length doubled, so area × 2².

practice2.q: Two similar triangles have areas 5 cm<sup>2</sup> and 45 cm<sup>2</sup>. What is the scale factor from the small triangle to the large one?
practice2.hint: Area factor = 45 ÷ 5 = 9 = k<sup>2</sup>. Take the square root.

fb.9: That is the area factor. k² = 9, so k = √9.

practice2.q: Two similar solids have surface areas in the ratio 1 : 16. Their volumes are in the ratio 1 : ?

fb.16: That is the area factor again. Find k = 4 first, then k³.
fb.256: You squared 16. Find k = √16 = 4, then cube it.

practice2.q: A cube of volume 64 cm<sup>3</sup> is reduced to a similar cube of volume 1 cm<sup>3</sup>. What is the scale factor? Type a fraction or decimal.
practice2.hint: Volume factor = 164 = k3. What number cubed is 164?

fb.1/64: That is the volume factor. k³ = 1/64, so take the cube root.
fb.1/8: That is the square root. Volume uses k³: take the cube root of 1/64.

practice3.q: A pizzeria prices pizzas by area. A 20 cm pizza costs $12. What should a similar 30 cm pizza cost, in dollars?

fb.18: You scaled the price by k. Pizza is an area: multiply by k² = 2.25.

practice3.q: Gold plating a 10 cm statuette costs $40. The plating cost depends on surface area. What does it cost to plate a similar 25 cm statue, in dollars?

fb.100: You multiplied by k. Plating covers a surface: use k² = 6.25.
fb.625: You used k³. Plating covers a surface (area), not a volume.

practice3.q: A 1 : 20 scale model of a yacht has a sail of area 300 cm<sup>2</sup>. What is the area of the real sail, in m<sup>2</sup>? (1 m<sup>2</sup> = 10 000 cm<sup>2</sup>)

fb.0.6: You multiplied by 20. The sail is an area: multiply by 20² = 400.
fb.120000: That is in cm². Divide by 10 000 to change to m².

practice3.q: A water tank holds 500 litres. A similar tank has every length 2 times as long. The water costs $0.30 per 100 litres. How much does it cost to fill the large tank, in dollars?

fb.3: You doubled the capacity. Capacity is a volume: × 2³ = 8.
fb.6: You used the area factor 4. Capacity is a volume: × 8.

exitProbs.q: A shape is enlarged with k = 3. The area is multiplied by what number?

fb.3: That is the scale factor. Area has two dimensions, so multiply by k × k.

exitProbs.q: A solid has volume 10 cm3. It is enlarged with k = 2. What is the new volume, in cm3?

fb.20: You multiplied by k. Volume has three dimensions: × 2³.
fb.40: You used the area factor. Volume factor is 2³ = 8.

exitProbs.q: Explain why doubling every length of a cube multiplies its volume by 8, not by 2.
exitProbs.hint: Think about the three dimensions of a cube, or count the small cubes in the I Do picture.
